batches.rationale: Foundational and room-platform epics whose Jira children are all Done and whose acceptance artifacts remain present in the current release.
User-facing room discovery, manifesto, and Wave-1 editorial epics whose Jira children are all Done and whose publication artifacts remain live.
Dependency-bearing geo, VMN and Wave-2 parents. KAN-9, KAN-84 and KAN-89 can close; KAN-140 remains In Progress until the explicitly blocked chronology child is resolved.
The complete Hanseatic programme is reconciled after all fourteen leaf tickets, seven parent outcomes and the production release evidence landed together.

epics.title: Foundations
acceptance: Project skeleton and TypeScript/Astro tooling are in place.
Shared design primitives are provided by the global token system.
Shared content primitives are enforced by the essay collection schema and registry.

epics.title: Portal Shell & Atlas Landing
acceptance: A single publication front door is generated at the root route.
Header, footer and layout provide consistent portal chrome.
Atlas and faceted essay landing pages are available through the shared shell.

epics.title: Legacy Essay Integration
acceptance: The four source essays resolve through the shared essay host route.
Raw legacy applications remain isolated under the embed boundary.
Publication metadata and shared portal navigation frame every essay.

epics.title: Room Taxonomy & Content Schema
acceptance: The seven-room taxonomy has one canonical data module.
Essay and section room fields are schema-validated.
Every published essay and deep-linked section is covered by room tests.

epics.title: Room Landing Pages & Cross-linking
acceptance: A rooms overview and one generated landing route per room are published.
Each room carries authored introductory copy from the canonical room data.
Badges, paths and related-content components connect essays and rooms.

epics.title: Search, Nav & Design System for Rooms
acceptance: Room identity participates in the global search index and search UI.
All seven rooms have canonical SVG glyphs.
Rooms are discoverable through the shared footer and About page.

epics.title: Manifesto Expansion (About)
acceptance: About functions as the publication manifesto rather than a placeholder.
Every Map Is an Argument is represented in the manifesto.
The Seduction of Precision is represented in the manifesto.

epics.title: Essay: Invisible Maps of Trade
acceptance: The Wave-1 Road anchor essay is published as native MDX.
Its interactive spine resolves the VMN route and commodity network.
The recurring Invisible Maps series shell links the published essays.

epics.title: Essay: Maps That Age
acceptance: The Wave-1 Archive anchor essay is published as native MDX.
Plate-state comparison is delivered as a dedicated interactive.
Cartometry evidence is exported and integrated into the essay argument.

epics.title: Essay: Invisible Maps of Religion
acceptance: The Wave-1 Theatre anchor essay is published as native MDX.
Sacred orientation is delivered as an accessible interactive.
The essay participates in the shared Invisible Maps series.

epics.title: Geo-Data Tier (GIS / Historical GIS)
acceptance: Serverless cloud-native vector layers support the Atlas map.
Layer metadata, temporal behavior and versioned publication are validated.
Gazetteer interoperability and exploratory historical overlays close the optional gaps.

epics.title: VMN c.1400 Atlas Layer
acceptance: The cosmography roadmap links the VMN Atlas layer to its detailed work.
The published VMN data track remains documented as the implementation umbrella.
Invisible Maps of Trade consumes and links back to the VMN Atlas layer.

epics.title: Wave 2 Essays
acceptance: The normalized Wave-2 backlog covers every listed essay outcome.
Eight native editorial essays are published with canonical room assignments.
Component assignment and editorial QA are release-gated.

epics.title: Routes (mude)
acceptance: Muda waypoint sequences, corrected sea paths, compiled routes and the first Atlas flip are complete.
The chronology handoff and discrepancy ledger explicitly preserve the evidence boundary.
The parent remains In Progress until page-level chronology verification and citations are available.

epics.title: Concept, corpus and rights
acceptance: Title, slug, AD 1150–1669 scope, room assignments, source schemas and stable identifiers are frozen in repository documentation.
Eight production witnesses include a hero and two fallbacks, cover every planned essay section and carry no unresolved P0 rights dependency.
The source-to-data-to-Atlas-to-native-MDX vertical slice builds without duplicating source geometry or dates in essay code.

epics.title: Historical research and evidence ledger
acceptance: High-importance chronological and institutional claims resolve to page- or folio-level evidence and a review decision.
Controlled terminology preserves participation uncertainty and rejects unsupported foundation, membership and dissolution claims.
Novgorod, Bergen, London and Bruges have reviewed multi-paragraph dossiers with primary witnesses and complete component payloads.

epics.title: Hanseatic places and institutions dataset
acceptance: Sixty EPSG:4326 place phases use stable IDs, controlled roles, participation classes and evidence joins without a boolean membership field.
All four Kontor hosts resolve to complete reviewed profiles and the required core cities are present.
GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf, generated essay JSON and the content-addressed manifest pass deterministic publication validation.

epics.title: Routes, commodities, privileges and build pipeline
acceptance: Seven evidence-labelled corridors include all four required cores without implying exact voyages or encoding unsupported volume.
Ten commodity families, twenty-two normalized joins and sixteen institutional events resolve to source and evidence rows.
The deterministic compiler validates schemas, enums, IDs, geometry, time, waypoints and provenance and records hashes and feature counts.

epics.title: Atlas integration and research reuse
acceptance: Places, routes and events are registered as temporal Atlas layers with evidence-legible styling and no territory polygon.
Feature panels expose provenance, notes, essay anchors and documentary links while historic and modern names remain searchable.
Typed deep links restore layer, feature and year state, and versioned citation/research-reuse metadata is covered by tests.

epics.title: Native essay and interactive components
acceptance: A 5,000–8,000-word native MDX essay follows the approved nine-section architecture.
Five generated-data interactives expose accessible controls, uncertainty language and static fallbacks.
Room metadata, search metadata, catalogue witnesses and claim-ledger references ship with the essay.

epics.title: Venice comparison, cross-linking and publication
acceptance: The comparison keeps VMN and HSE sources separate while explaining their different political geometries.
At least three reciprocal incoming and three outgoing links connect the essay, comparison and catalogue.
Catalogue, bibliography, social assets and production QA are recorded in a validated release manifest.
